title: Compact encryption evidence archiver for cross-region residency certification
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Auditors and customers require compact, verifiable bundles that prove where tenant encryption keys and ciphertext were resident during retention windows. Current exports are large, noisy, and not reproducible across regions, which slows compliance reviews and increases manual effort.

Goal: Build an evidence archiver that produces reproducible, compact artifacts per-tenant and per-period that are signed by our HSM/KMS signing keys, include a Merkle root index of included records, and encode residency and retention metadata to support automated verification and long-term archival. The artifact should be small enough to store in compliance buckets and easy for external auditors to verify with a provided verifier tool.

Scope:
- Collect HSM/KMS rotation logs, wrapping key attestations, and per-request residency metadata for a configurable time window.
- Normalize timestamps to UTC and canonicalize region naming to avoid diff issues.
- Create Merkle-indexed manifests so auditors can request compact inclusion proofs for individual records.
- Create a signing step that uses the tenant-wrapped KMS key to produce an artifact signature and an operator signature from an HSM key where available.
- Provide a CLI verifier that checks signatures, Merkle proofs, and that retention/residency predicates match provided policies.
- Export formats: compressed .tar.gz with JSONL blobs and a compact index, plus a human-readable summary for quick triage.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact generator runs as a scheduled job and produces one artifact per customer per 24h window
Artifacts include a Merkle root index and per-record cryptographic inclusion proofs
Artifacts are signed with both the service HSM operator key and the tenant KEK signing key when tenant KEK is present
CLI verifier accepts an artifact and returns PASS/FAIL with a short error log and verification of residency timestamps and region canonicalization
Artifacts size reduction of at least 60% vs raw export for median-tenant test dataset
End-to-end E2E test that verifies reproducibility: given same source logs, artifact binary is identical across two runs
technical_notes: Use a streaming JSONL writer to avoid loading full windows into memory
Merkle tree built over canonicalized record digests (sha256 of stable JSON serialization)
Sign with HSM via PKCS#11 adapter used in runtime; fall back to KMS sign API for hosted customers without HSM
Store artifacts in compliance S3 bucket with lifecycle policy and immutable tags
Expose a short-lived presigned URL for auditor downloads; track access in audit log
Retention-aware packaging: include retention_policy_id and expiry timestamps so verifier can assert whether records were still within retention at the time of the snapshot
decisions: Chosen artifact format: tar.gz of JSONL + compact index to balance human-readability and size
Use Merkle indexing for inclusion proofs rather than per-record signatures to reduce signing overhead
Canonicalization format: sort JSON object keys, normalize timestamps to RFC3339 UTC, map region aliases to canonical region IDs
Verifier will be distributed as a small Go binary to avoid environment deps and to support reproducible build verification
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signing throughput for large tenants could bottleneck job - mitigate by batching Merkle sign step and using operator HSM for only roots
Risk: Replay or tampering attacks if artifacts are not pinned - mitigate via cryptographic signatures and storing signature metadata in our audit index
Risk: Region canonicalization drift - mitigate by pinning canonical map as a versioned config and including the map version in artifacts
Risk: Legal requests require more granular evidence - provide hooks to produce ad-hoc inclusion proofs on demand and expand scheduled windows
